blogs.title: When Breathing Becomes Automatic Failure: Central Hypoventilation Masquerading as Anxiety in Chiari Malformation
blogs.description: Explore the rare but life-threatening presentation of Chiari Malformation Type I (CMI) as acquired central hypoventilation syndrome ('Ondine's Curse'). This post analyzes the dissociation between voluntary and automatic breathing, explaining why patients may remain unaware of severe hypoxia due to disrupted brainstem afferent pathways. We will discuss the 'airport episode' vignette where distraction precipitated desaturation without dyspnea, highlighting the danger of attributing these symptoms to psychiatric causes.

blogs.title: The Choking Mystery: Why Normal Endoscopy Should Trigger a Neurological Workup for Dysphagia
blogs.description: Focus on the diagnostic pitfall of unexplained oropharyngeal dysphagia. This article breaks down the clinical differentiation between mechanical obstruction (which yields positive endoscopic findings) and neurogenic causes like CMI (where endoscopy is normal). We will review the statistics linking CMI to swallowing dysfunction and emphasize that choking on both solids and liquids equally is a red flag for brainstem compression, urging clinicians to look up toward the foramen magnum when GI workups fail.

blogs.title: Revisiting Old Scans: The Diagnostic Power of Retrospective Imaging Review in Delayed Diagnoses
blogs.description: A practical guide on leveraging historical data in complex cases. Using this case's timeline, we examine how a CT scan taken 14 years ago—initially read as normal—held the key to the diagnosis upon re-evaluation. This post discusses the concept of 'overlooked anatomy,' emphasizing that crowded foramina and tonsillar descent can be subtle. It provides a framework for when and how to request retrospective reviews of old imaging in patients with long-standing, unexplained neurological or respiratory complaints.

blogs.title: Beyond the Apnea-Hypopnea Index: Pitfalls of Type III Sleep Studies in Suspected Brainstem Pathology
blogs.description: Critique the limitations of portable sleep studies (Type III) in detecting central hypoventilation syndromes. We analyze why this patient's AHI appeared deceptively mild (6.0) despite documented severe desaturations, focusing on how calculating AHI based on total recording time versus true sleep time masks central events. The post argues for the necessity of full polysomnography (Type I) with EEG and capnography when brainstem compression is suspected, ensuring accurate quantification of central apneas vs. obstructive events.

blogs.title: Trauma Unmasking Tonsillar Herniation: Congenital vs. Acquired Etiologies in Chiari Syndrome
blogs.description: Delve into the pathophysiological debate surrounding Chiari Malformation Type I etiology in adults. Is this a congenital anomaly exacerbated by trauma, or a true traumatic acquisition? This discussion explores recent literature suggesting CMI can develop secondary to head injury due to altered CSF dynamics or craniosynostosis-like changes. We will weigh the evidence from this case regarding timing (symptoms starting immediately post-accident) against congenital predisposition theories and its implications for surgical candidacy.
